newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has earmarked 75.7 billion pesos for anti-poverty projects this year, budget secretary Salvador Enriquez said. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Congressman Rolando Andaya, chairman of the congressional appropriation committee, blamed his Senate counterpart for delaying the approval of the 1997 budget. (TODAY)
- Cabinet members who are planning to run for president next year need not resign just yet, presidential assistant for political affairs Gabriel Caludio said. (PILIPIPNE STAR)

- Fugitive congressman Romeo Jalosjos, who was reported to have fled the country, is still hiding in one of the exclusive residential villages in Manila, police sources said. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Guoco Holdings signed a memorandum of understanding with Premiere Beverages Philippines Inc to buy 51 percent of Pepsi-Cola Products Phils Inc, the local franchise holder of Pepsi products. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The Bureau of Internal Revenue is not keen on retaining the 20 percent withholding tax slapped on reverse repurchase agreements as a permanent measure. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The Board of Investments will widen the scope of environmental projects that will be eligible for incentives under the proposed 1997 Investment Priorities Plan (INQUIRER)
- The government has built up its deposits with the Central Bank to 30 bilion pesos at the end of 1996, exceeding its full-year deposit target of 29.7 bilion pesos. (TODAY)
